clue.text: What would pet's groom give for somewhere to rest, finally?

definitions.text: What would pet's groom give for somewhere to rest, finally?

parts.words: What would pet's groom give for somewhere to rest, finally?
parts.note: a pet (a cat) plus a groom (a comb) gives the pun ..., an underground burial place where the dead rest for good

explanation.surface: A riddle about what grooming a pet might produce, apparently asking for a cosy bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pet's groom' as CAT plus A COMB: the cat's grooming tool. 'Rest, finally' points to the last rest, burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground galleries with tombs are the final resting place of the dead.

clue.text: Pen he used to write down score

definitions.meaning: a pen is an enclosure for animals

definitions.text: he used to write down score
definitions.meaning: John ..., the American composer (died 1992), who wrote musical scores

explanation.surface: A man who once kept a tally with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a tally or twenty, but it is a musical score, and 'he used to write' is a composer from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for animals is a synonym, and John Cage was a famous experimental composer.

clue.text: Polish, perhaps, donor gave in error for a certain type of panelling?

parts.note: Polish is an example of a language, also called a tongue

indicators.note: something done in error is mistaken, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A donor who, perhaps Polish, mistakenly paid for some wall panelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb (to shine wood), but with its capital it is the language. 'in error' rearranges DONOR GAVE into AND GROOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards joined by a ridge fitting into a slot form a common style of wooden panelling.

clue.text: Arrangement for free distribution of Mirror by Labour

parts.note: to mirror something is to copy it
the British Labour Party is on the political left

explanation.surface: Labour arranges for the Daily Mirror, a left-leaning tabloid, to be given away free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' looks like the newspaper, but it is the verb to copy. COPYLEFT is a licence letting software or writing be freely shared and changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensing scheme lets a work be freely copied and redistributed on the same terms.

clue.text: Upset without end that the Queen's going?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone upset at an aimless plan, wondering what the monarch is saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen is not the monarch but a female cat, so what she is 'going' (saying) is a cat's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and a cat's cry is its characteristic call.

clue.text: Lawyer in centre cut short bluff reformer

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word lawyer are used
the last letter of the synonym is lopped off

parts.note: a bluff is a steep headland or cliff

explanation.surface: A blunt lawyer cut off in mid-sentence by a reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like an adjective (blunt), but it is the noun, a cliff. John Wyclif (also Wycliffe) was the 14th-century English church reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wyclif was an English theologian who pressed for church reform and an English Bible.

clue.text: More than one tough year: pupil once making ends meet with shillings

parts.note: a former pupil is an old boy, OB; set it end to end with its mirror image so the two B ends meet, giving OBBO
S is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: A hard year for a former schoolboy struggling to make ends meet on a few shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making ends meet' sounds like scraping by, but it joins OB to its reverse so the Bs touch. Shillings were pre-1971 British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbo is British slang for a loutish thug, so the plural means several toughs.

clue.text: When lacking space, I role play

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver to close the gap between the two words that follow, joining them into one string

parts.note: a reverse clue: with no space between them, the two words make IROLE, which is LO (look) written backwards inside IRE (anger); 'When lacking space' tells the solver to close the gap

explanation.surface: Someone saying that, short of room, they will play the part themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions, builds 'I role' without its space. 'Play' is the definition: John Osborne's 1956 drama.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne's 1956 drama about Jimmy Porter is the classic 'angry young man' stage work.

clue.text: Place Lot's (ex-)wife turned to

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Bible echo: the place where Lot's wife, now his ex, was turned into salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned to' recalls Lot's wife turned to a pillar of salt; 'turned' rearranges LOTS EX WIFE. FELIXSTOWE is a port town in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Felixstowe is a town and major container port on the Suffolk coast, so a location.

clue.text: Shallow type involved in leak

indicators.note: one word is wrapped up inside another

parts.note: to leak is to seep
a type is a kind

explanation.surface: A shallow sort of person who got mixed up in a leak to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' looks like being implicated in a scandal, but it places one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only surface-level, as in beauty being superficial, lacks depth.

clue.text: A no-good, mean Greek covers escape route from vessel

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap round and cover the rest

parts.note: NG is short for no good
to mean to do something is to plan it

explanation.surface: A worthless, mean-spirited Greek guarding a ship's exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but it is the verb to intend.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank laid from ship to shore is the way passengers get off a boat.

clue.text: Train company once getting fuel to overheat?

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former nationalised railway
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A former railway firm taking on fuel and running too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran trains in Britain until privatisation in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill fiercely, or figuratively to swelter, is to be exposed to great heat.

clue.text: Sign edict

definitions.meaning: Taurus, the zodiac sign of the ...
a papal decree, so called from its seal

explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is a star sign shown as the animal, and a pope's formal decree has the same name.

clue.text: Plants here light punch

parts.note: a light is a window pane, as in a leaded light
to punch is to box

explanation.surface: A light punch, apparently a gentle jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light punch' reads as a soft blow, but 'light' is a noun, a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough on a sill is a place where flowers are grown.

clue.text: Cover this with loose change

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay for something with spare coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose change' looks like coins; 'loose' shuffles COVER THIS plus W, leaving 'change' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A changeover from one system to another is a synonym for a change.

clue.text: Dock manager travelling far to stop person complaining

indicators.note: the shuffled letters stop up the middle of the other word, like a plug

parts.note: a whinger is someone who moans

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dock boss travelling a long way to silence a complainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' makes ARF. 'Whinger' is British slang for a moaner; a wharfinger is an old trade word, fairly guessable from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf owner or keeper is in charge of a quay where ships load and unload.

clue.text: Reluctant to give a single person reason for alarm or relief on aircraft?

definitions.text: reason for alarm or relief on aircraft?

parts.note: near means stingy, unwilling to part with money
Miss is the title for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A stingy flyer who won't explain anything to a lone passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old word for mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Two planes almost colliding cause alarm, then relief that no crash happened.

clue.text: Burns for one second by crash site

parts.note: to crash is slang for to sleep, and a cot is a bed to sleep in

explanation.surface: Something burning for a second beside the wreckage of a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' is Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, not fire; 'crash site' is a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was born in Ayrshire, so he is an example of a Scotsman.

clue.text: Fury with lift breaking down, becoming a pest

indicators.note: things breaking down fall to pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone furious that the lift has broken down, turning into a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny insect that swarms round ripe produce is a household and orchard nuisance.

clue.text: On which you'll find one solo love song and dance

parts.words: On which you'll find one solo
parts.note: 'on your tod' is British slang for alone (from rhyming slang Tod Sloan = own)
love is nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A lone performer of a love song with a dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: British 'on your tod' means on your own, so TOD is what someone solo is on. 'Song and dance' is a fuss, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is an idiom for a commotion or fuss over something.

clue.text: Sort of TV journal containing variable opinion

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a journal is a newspaper
Y is a variable in algebra
an opinion is a view

explanation.surface: A television magazine running a column of mixed opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' is the algebra sense, a letter such as x or y, not 'changeable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Television where viewers are charged for each programme they watch is one kind of TV service.

clue.text: Couple set on making the last hours

indicators.note: the word's final letter is swapped for the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A pair who prepared to make the final hours count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making the last hours' turns the final K of ATTACK into H.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or fasten them together.

clue.text: King visiting entertained by book

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a host, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: to have people round is to entertain them
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
by means multiplied by, as in two times three

explanation.surface: A king on a visit is entertained by someone with a book.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside HAD; 'by' is the times sign in multiplication. The answer is a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens's 1854 novel set in industrial Coketown is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Don, maybe, sister's clothing I brought up

indicators.note: the outer word dresses, or wraps, the inner one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A university don, perhaps, wearing his sister's clothing he once picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' makes ENO. 'Don' is a Spanish gentleman's title, not a lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is a Spanish honorific, so a Don is an example of a Spanish gentleman or Mr.

clue.text: Man's daughter getting out of bed

indicators.note: the abbreviation leaves the word, which loses that letter

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A man's daughter climbing out of bed in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: D leaves DIVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian name, the equivalent of John, is an example of a man's name.

clue.text: Old money from which you'll no change either way

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, unchanged in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An old coin that won't get you any change whichever way you pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no change' looks like shopping; it means the letters are the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee is an obsolete currency unit.

clue.text: Instrument to break after putting out second note

TE is a note of the sol-fa scale, here the second note in the word after LA

explanation.definitionFit: A viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin.

clue.text: Address, in the US, firearm issue

definitions.meaning: an American form of address, a jocular exclamation to a rascal
the issue, or offspring, of a gun

explanation.surface: An American speech on gun issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a political topic, but it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The American expression is a mock-insulting way to address someone, and literally means a child of a gun.

clue.text: Parrot again eclipsed by screech owl

indicators.note: the letters are obscured within the longer phrase, eclipsed by it

explanation.surface: A parrot outshone once more by a noisy owl.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'screech owl'. 'Parrot' is the verb to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat, so parroting again is repeating a sound once more.

clue.text: New Year's Jumbo, briefly, with anything badly defined?

indicators.note: here the shortened word is with, holding, the shuffled one inside
a word made brief loses its last letter

parts.note: jumbo means great in size

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A New Year jumbo crossword, briefly, where nothing is clearly defined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives EYAR and 'briefly' gives GREA; 'Jumbo' is not the elephant but an adjective, very large.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambiguous situation with no clear rules is one not falling neatly into either category.
